facts.text: The Indische Buurt’s streets are named after islands and other places from the former Dutch East Indies, giving the neighborhood its distinctive name.
Developed east of the Oosterpark on reclaimed polder land, the Indische Buurt grew to house factory, shipyard, and industry workers.
Muiderpoort Station opened in 1939, breaking the Indische Buurt’s isolation behind the railway that once separated it from the rest of Amsterdam.
Today Javastraat hosts a lively market where halal vendors and international eateries reflect the neighborhood’s multicultural heritage.
The 2010 renewal of Timorplein introduced a new cultural hub with a theater, hostel, and conference rooms, reshaping the area’s social scene.
